G9301.definition: to dine  or sup with  another, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus); μετά τινων (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to dine  or sup with others , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; οἱ ξυνδειπνοῦντες the members of a picnic party , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9302.definition:
1. to join two and two, couple , (Aristotle Philosopher): —;Pass. to be coupled with something else , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. in Pass. to be coupled, to pair , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9303.definition:
1. of Place, near together , (Thucydides), etc.; ς. ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοις (Aristotle Philosopher):—; τὸ ς. nearness, proximity , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. of Time, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. of Quality, οἱ ς. persons of similar rank , (Aristotle Philosopher); ἡ ς. αἰτία the proximate  cause, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9307.definition: to rear up along with  or together , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to grow up with , τινί (Euripides) (ML)

G9308.definition:
1. to draw together, to draw up, contract , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to draw out along with, to help to draw out , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9309.definition: to assist in raising : Pass., aor1 participle συνεξαρθείς being lifted up at once , (Plutarch); being excited at the same time , (Lucian) (ML)

G9310.definition: Dep.:—; to go  or come out with , τινι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9313.definition: Dep. to be privy to , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9315.gloss: to join in making an attack
G9315.definition:
1. to help in putting on , (Plutarch) 
2. Mid. to join in attacking , τινι (Thucydides); ξ. τῷ ἔργῳ ̀ 6 6̀ το fall to the work together , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9321.definition: of like  or equal age , Lat. aequalis, a playmate, comrade, [6th/5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9324.definition:
1. a putting together, composition, combination , (Plato Philosophus); γραμμάτων συνθέσεις, i. e. syllables and words, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;also, of an author's composition , (Isocrates Orator) 
2. metaphorically, like συνθεσία, an agreement, treaty , (Pindar) 
3. Lat. synthesis was a suit of clothes , (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus); especially a loose gown , worn at dinner-parties, (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus) (ML)

G9325.definition:
1. put together, composite, compound , (Plato Philosophus): complex , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. put together, fictitious , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. metaphorically agreed upon , ἐκ συνθέτου by agreement , Lat. ex composito, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9326.definition:
1. a composition , of words and sentences, (Lucian) 
2. a conventional agreement, convention, compact , (Plato Philosophus); ἐκ συνθήκης, ex composito, by agreement , (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ συνθήκην conventionally , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. the article of a compact  or treaty , (Thucydides):—;mostly in plural the articles of agreement , and collectively, a contract, compact, covenant, treaty , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; συνθήκας ποιέεσθαί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν συνθηκῶν according to the covenant , (Isocrates Orator); κατὰ τὰς ς. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9327.definition:
1. knowing along with  another, conscious , ὡς θεοὶ ξυνίστορες as the gods are witnesses , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
2. with accusative (with the verbal construction), πολλὰ συνίστορα κακά conscious of  many evils, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9332.definition:
1. to make to live with , (Isocrates Orator); ς. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to give  him one's daughter in marriage , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to combine in one city, unite under a capital  or metropolis , ξ. πάντας (i.e. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας)) (Thucydides):—;Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having been regularly formed , opposite to κατὰ κώμας οἰκίζεσθαι, (Thucydides) 
3. to join in peopling  or colonising  a country, (Euripides) 
4. generally to unite, associate , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9335.definition:
1. that which is put together in order : 
2. a body  of troops, squadron, contingent , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. the constitution of a state , ς. πολιτείας a form  of constitution, (Isocrates Orator) 
4. an arrangement of musical notes , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine , (Plutarch) 
6. = σύνταξις II. 3, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9336.definition:
1. a putting together, arranging, arrangement, organisation, order , (Thucydides): rule , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. a systematic treatise , (Aristotle Philosopher): a narrative , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. grammatical construction, syntax , (Lucian) 
4. a body of troops , ἡ εἰς μυρίους ς. their contingent  towards 10, 000, (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. a covenant, contract , (Demosthenes Orator) 
6. an assigned impost, contribution , (Demosthenes Orator) 
7. a payment, allowance, pension , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9337.definition: to throw all together into confusion, to confound, disturb, trouble , Lat. conturbare, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;Pass., αἰθὴρ πόντῳ ξυντετάρακται air is confounded with  sea, (Aeschulus Tragicus): to be thrown into confusion , of soldiers, (Thucydides); of social order, (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically of persons, to be confounded, greatly troubled, much distressed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9344.definition: to weave together : metaphorically to frame with art, devise cunningly , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ὥστε ταῦτα συνυφανθῆναι so that this web was woven , i. e. this business undertaken, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9348.definition:
1. a pipe : 
2. a musical pipe, a shepherd's pipe, Panspipe , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
3. anything like a pipe : 
4. a spear-case , = δορατοθήκη, (Iliad by Homer) 
5. the hole in the nave of a wheel , [variant datesTragica Adespota 
6. a duct  or channel  in the body, in plural the nostrils , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
 (ML)

G9349.definition:
1. to play the  σῦριγξ, to pipe , (Euripides); with accusative cognate, συρίζων ὑμεναίους (Euripides) 
2. to whistle, hiss , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with accusative cognate, συρίζων φόνον hissing forth  murder, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. to hiss  an actor, Lat. explodere, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9351.definition: to sew  or stitch together, sew up , Lat. consuo, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9352.definition: one who lives in the same tent, a messmate , Lat. contubernalis, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9353.definition:
1. to shade quite over, throw a shade over, shade closely  or thickly , (Hesiod); γένυν ς., i. e.to get a beard, (Euripides): metaphorically, συσκηνῶσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. intransitive to be thick-shaded , (Euripides) (ML)

G9354.definition: closely shaded, thickly shaded , (Xenophon Historicus); σύσκιόν τι a closely-shaded place , (Lucian) (ML)

G9355.definition: to grow quite dark : impersonal, συσκοτάζει it grows dark , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9356.definition:
1. to draw together, draw up, contract , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to draw together  by stitching, sew together , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Mid. to draw along with one , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9359.definition:
1. a putting together, composition , (Aristotle Philosopher); ς. προσώπου a studied expression  of countenance, of Pericles, (Plutarch) 
2. a bringing together, introduction, recommendation , (Polybius Historicus) 
3.  συνίσταμαι); a standing together, meeting : in hostile sense, close combat, conflict , (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically, ς. γνώμης a conflict  of mind, intense anxiety, (Thucydides) 
4. a meeting, a knot of men , (Euripides); κατὰ ξυστάσεις γιγνόμενοι forming into knots , (Thucydides): a political union , (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. friendship  or alliance , (Polybius Historicus): a conspiracy , (Plutarch) 
6. construction, structure, constitution , (Plato Philosophus): absolute a political constitution , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. metaphorically of the mind, ς. φρενῶν contraction, sternness, sullenness , (Euripides) (ML)

G9361.definition:
anything twisted up together: a body of men, a crowd, concourse , (Polybius Historicus) 
from συστρέφω (ML)

G9364.definition: to be gangrened , ἐσφακέλισε τὸ ὀστέον (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9365.definition:
1. likely to make one stumble  or trip : metaphorically slippery, perilous, dangerous , Lat. lubricus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; σφαλερόν [ ἐστι], with infinitive, it is dangerous  to . ., (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2.  σφάλλομαι); ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφ. σύμμαχοι (Demosthenes Orator) 
 (ML)

G9366.definition:
1. Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—; to make to fall, throw down, overthrow , properly by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling , (Homer), etc.; σφ. ναῦς to throw  her on her beam-ends , (Plutarch); ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην throws  him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be tripped up , (Aristophanes Comicus); of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος reeling, staggering , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. generally, to cause to fall, overthrow, defeat , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be overthrown, to fall, fail, be undone, become helpless , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; τόδ᾽ ἐσφάλη this mishap took place , (Sophocles Tragicus); οὔ τι μὴ σφαλῶ γ᾽ ἐν σοί I shall  not fail  in thy business, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. to baffle, foil, balk, disappoint , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to err, go wrong, be mistaken , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. the Pass. is also used with genitive rei, to be balked of  or foiled in  a thing, ἦ καὶ πατήρ τι σφάλλεται βουλευμάτω; (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφάλλεσθαι γάμου (Euripides); τῆς δόξης (Thucydides) (ML)

G9368.definition:
1. to sling, to use the sling , (Thucydides) 
2. to strike by slinging , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 
3. to throw as from a sling :—;Pass., (Euripides) 
4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro , (Euripides) 
from σφενδόνη (ML)

G9369.definition:
1. Lat. funda (the ς being lost), a sling , (Iliad by Homer): metaphorically, σφενδόνας ἀπ᾽ εὐμέτρου with well-measured throw, as from a sling , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. the hoop  of a ring in which the stone was set  as in a sling, especially the broader part round the stone , as in Lat. funda for pala annuli , (Euripides) 
3. the stone  or bullet of the sling , (Xenophon Historicus); τοιαύταις σφ., of hailstones, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9373.definition: to bind tight, bind fast , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9374.definition:
1. vehement, violent, excessive , (Thucydides), etc. 
2. of men, violent, impetuous , (Plato Philosophus): also strong, robust , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9375.definition:
1. a vertebra , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in plural the backbone, spine , or the neck , (Euripides) 
2. Lat. verticillus, the round weight attached to a spindle, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9376.definition:
1. a hammer , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a beetle, mallet , for breaking clods of earth, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9379.definition:
1. properly to let loose : hence to slit, open , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. φλέβα to open  a vein, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—;of flowers, σχ. κάλυκας [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. to let fall, drop , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. to let go , σχάσας τὴν φροντίδα having let  the mind go, given  it play , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. τὰς μηχανάς to let off  the engines, (Plutarch) 
4. to check, stop, stay , Lat. inhibere, κώπαν σχάσον, i. e. cease rowing, (Pindar); σχάσον ὄμμα lower  thine eyes, (Euripides):—;Mid., σχασάμενος τὴν ἱππικήν having dropt  one's horsemanship, "given up the turf," (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9380.definition:
1. a raft, float  (such as was made off-hand , compare σχέδιος II), (Odyssey by Homer); generally, a boat, ship , (Euripides) 
2. a bridge of boats , of the bridge of Xerxes, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9382.definition:
1. a piece of wood cleft off, a lath, splinter , Lat. scindula, (Odyssey by Homer): in plural cleft wood, fire-wood , (Homer) 
2. an arrow , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
 (ML)

G9385.definition: a measured out line; a piece of measured out land

G9386.gloss: a piece of measured out land
G9386.definition: a fencing with ropes : in plural roping, rope-fences , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9387.definition:
1. a rush , Lat. juncus, scirpus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. a reed , used as an arrow  or javelin , (Batrachomyomachia) 
3. a place where rushes grow, a rushbed , (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. a rush-rope , and generally, a rope, cord , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) 
5. a fence  round a garden, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
6. a land-measure , = 2 Persian parasangs, = 60 stades, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9388.definition:
1. one who lives at ease , (Plutarch) 
2. as adjective leisurely, idle , βίος (Plutarch) (ML)

G9389.definition:
1. to make into a body, to consolidate, organise , (Polybius Historicus) 
2. to provide with bodily strength, to recruit , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9391.definition:
1. a heap , Lat. acervus, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. generally, a heap, quantity , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9394.definition:
1. a band, riband, fillet , especially a head-band , worn in sign of victory, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
2. a strip  or tongue of land , (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

G9395.definition: fit for ordering  or arranging , especially in war, τ. ἀνήρ a tactician , (Xenophon Historicus); τακτικὸν ἡγεῖσθαί τι to think it a good piece of tactics , (Xenophon Historicus); οἱ τ. ἀριθμοί the regular battalions, (Xenophon Historicus): τὰ τακτικά the art of drawing up soldiers in array, tactics , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9397.definition:
suffering, wretched , Lat. miser, (Odyssey by Homer); ὦ τάλαιν᾽ ἐγώ (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὦ τάλαν (Sophocles Tragicus);—;with genitive causae, τάλαιν᾽ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως wretched that I am  for this insolence, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in bad sense, τάλαν wretch!  (Odyssey by Homer)—;comparative τᾶλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾶλάντατος, η, ον, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 τᾶλα_; doric also τᾶλᾶς: vocative τάλᾶν. (ML)

G9398.definition:
1. one who carves and distributes, a dispenser , (Iliad by Homer):—;of Zeus, as the dispenser  of all things to men, (Iliad by Homer); so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων (Odyssey by Homer):—;of kings or rulers, a controller, director , (Pindar); τ. κώμων master  of the revels, (Pindar); τ. Διός the priest  of Zeus, (Pindar): τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, (Pindar); οἶκος τ. στεφάνων that hath store  of crowns, (Pindar); τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ. controller  both of his desire and of fortune, (Thucydides); τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in Prose, a controller  of payments, treasurer , (Herdotus Historicus); τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ the controller  of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. at Rome, the quaestor , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9399.definition:
1. to be controller  of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with genitive, τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of  the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. at Rome, to be quaestor , (Plutarch) 
3. transitive to deal out, dispense , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have  the laws dealt out , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control  the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 
4. of keeping house, to regulate, manage , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed  or possessed  by one, (Pindar) 
5. to store up , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of  it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)
